title: Count Prefix and Suffix Pairs I
statement: Given an array of strings `words`, count the index pairs `(i, j)` with `i < j` such that `words[i]` is **both** a prefix of `words[j]` and a suffix of `words[j]`. A word counts as a prefix and a suffix of itself, so two equal words form such a pair. Return that count.
constraints: words[i] contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

There are at most 50 words of at most 10 letters, so at most 1,225 pairs, and each check touches at most 20 characters. Simply trying every pair `i < j` and asking whether `words[i]` sits at both ends of `words[j]` is fast and impossible to get wrong. (The harder version of this problem, with up to 10^5 words, needs a trie over (first letter, last letter) pairs; here enumeration is the right tool.)

## Approach

1. Set `count` to 0.
2. For every later index `j`, take `word = words[j]`.
3. For every earlier index `i < j`, take `piece = words[i]`.
4. If `word` starts with `piece` and also ends with `piece`, add 1 to `count`.
5. Return `count`.

## Example 1, step by step

`words = ["a","aba","ababa","aa"]`.

- `j = 1` (`"aba"`): `"a"` is at both ends, `count = 1`.
- `j = 2` (`"ababa"`): `"a"` fits, and `"aba"` is both its first and last three letters, `count = 3`.
- `j = 3` (`"aa"`): `"a"` fits (`count = 4`); `"aba"` and `"ababa"` are longer than `"aa"`, so `startsWith` fails.

The answer is `4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n² · L), with `n` words of length at most `L`: every pair is checked once, in O(L).
- Space: O(1) besides the input.

## Pitfalls

- The order matters: `words[i]` must be the earlier word and the shorter (or equal) one; `["aa", "a"]` gives 0, not 1.
- Being only a prefix (`"ab"` in `"abc"`) or only a suffix is not enough; both must hold.
- Equal words do count, since a word is a prefix and a suffix of itself.
- The prefix and suffix may overlap inside `words[j]`, as `"aba"` does in `"ababa"`; do not require them to be separate.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `count` | pairs found so far |
| `j`, `word` | index and text of the later word, the one that must contain the other at both ends |
| `i`, `piece` | index and text of the earlier word being tested |

narration.3: Pick the later word of the pair, at index j.
narration.4: word is the string that must hold the other one at both of its ends.
narration.5: Try every earlier index i, so that i < j always holds.
narration.6: piece is the candidate prefix and suffix.
narration.7: It counts only when word both starts and ends with piece.
narration.8: Both checks passed: count the pair (i, j).
narration.12: Every pair has been checked; return the total.
